pm_structure.summary: General account (C$165bn, Mar 2026) is managed by SLC Management, Sun Life's wholly owned alternatives/fixed-income manager, inside the Sun Life Asset Management pillar (Pres. Tom Murphy, 2026); the insurer's CIO (Randy Brown) sets ALM/SAA and oversees SLC as manager (CIO placement inferred).
manager_entities: Sun Life Asset Management (pillar from 2026-01-01: MFS, SLC Management, Aditya Birla SL AMC stake, PRT business)

SLC Management (Sun Life Capital Management) - SLC Fixed Income (ex Ryan Labs), BentallGreenOak (BGO, real estate), Crescent Capital (private credit), InfraRed Capital Partners (infrastructure), Advisors Asset Management (AAM, US retail distribution)
MFS Investment Management (third-party; does not manage GA)
bullets: SLC Management: C$260bn third-party + C$165bn Sun Life general account (Mar 2026); GA mandates are the anchor client and seed capital for SLC strategies.
CIO Randy Brown's Office of the CIO retains ALM, SAA and manager oversight (inferred from bios); day-to-day public FI, RE, private credit, infra run by SLC affiliates.
Jan 1 2026 reorganisation: Sun Life Asset Management pillar formalized under Tom Murphy: MFS, SLC, ABSL AMC stake (from Asia) and PRT/DB Solutions (from Canada).
Mar 30 2026: SLC bought remaining 44% of BGO (C$1.59bn) and 49% of Crescent (C$829m) - affiliates now 100% owned; SLC management equity plan up to 25%.
Jul 2 2026: SLC acquired Bell Partners (US multifamily, US$350m); Aug 2026: SLC named lead asset manager for Wilton Re / Windsor Life Re partnership (up to US$10bn).

rotation_commentary.text: Mortgages & loans 30% of GA invested assets (loans C$45.8bn, 96% investment grade); private fixed income remains the main spread sleeve via SLC Fixed Income.
ABS C$14.2bn = 17% of debt securities; growing structured credit through SLC/Crescent capabilities.
Investment properties C$9.4bn (5%); real estate experience negative in 2025, exposure held steady while office weighting is reduced (BGO-managed).
Buy-ups of BGO and Crescent (Q1 2026) deepen in-house private markets origination for the GA; SLC 2026 outlook stresses private credit and infrastructure growth.
Wilton Re/Windsor Life Re partnership (Aug 2026) adds third-party insurance balance sheets for SLC to manage - asset-intensive reinsurance as a growth channel.
DB Solutions (Canadian PRT) moved into SLAM Jan 2026; 2025 PRT market slower, so PRT-driven long-duration asset demand modest in 2025-26.

target_allocations.target: No numeric target allocation disclosed. Dec 2025 mix: cash 7%, debt 43%, equities 6%, mortgages & loans 30%, derivatives 1%, investment properties 5%, other 8%.
Underlying EPS growth 10%+, underlying ROE 20%+, dividend payout 40-50%, leverage <=25%.

Wilton Re / Windsor Life Re partnership: US$900m capital commitment, SLC lead asset manager, up to US$10bn (asset-intensive reinsurance platform).
Investments in SLC-managed funds (BGO, Crescent, InfraRed) as seed/co-invest; amounts not separately disclosed.
SLEECS innovative Tier 1 trust (Sun Life Capital Trust) C$200m; LRCN limited recourse trust holding C$1bn preferred shares.

deals.text: Acquired majority stake in Advisors Asset Management (AAM), US retail distribution for SLC; completed 2023-02-01.
Acquired Dialogue Health Technologies (to 95% from 23%, cash C$272m); completed 2023-10-03.
Increased stake in Bowtie (HK digital insurer); Q3 2025 gain C$176m.
AAM + Scotia Global Wealth distribution partnership (US retail alternatives).
Bought remaining 44% of BGO (C$1.59bn) and 49% of Crescent (C$829m); completed 2026-03-30; Q1 charge ~C$236m.
SLC acquired Bell Partners (US multifamily operator) for US$350m; closed 2026-07-02.
Wilton Re / Windsor Life Re strategic partnership (2026-08-25): US$900m capital, SLC lead asset manager, up to US$10bn; advisers Jefferies, Sidley Austin.
Agreed to take majority of Malaysia JV (Sun Life Malaysia) for ~C$240m; expected close late 2026.

bank_relationships.text: Bancassurance: CIMB Niaga 15-year exclusive (Indonesia), plus bank partners in Philippines, Vietnam, India (Aditya Birla JV), Malaysia (CIMB).
Canadian bank syndicate (RBC lead; BMO, TD, Scotia, CIBC rotating) on all CAD subordinated issues 2022-2026.

appetite: Board-approved Risk Appetite Policy sets capital, earnings-volatility, liquidity and reputational limits; risk limits cascade to business groups.
Market-risk appetite expressed via sensitivity limits (equity, rates, credit spreads, real estate) and LICAT-based capital-at-risk measures.
Three-tier risk framework: Risk Appetite Policy, Risk Management Framework, risk-specific policies (credit, market, liquidity, insurance, operational).
governance: Board Risk Committee oversees risk framework; Executive Risk Committee oversees capital/risk; CRO Jacques Goulet (EVP, 2026) with segment risk officers.
Three Lines of Defence model: business groups (1st), Risk Management/Compliance (2nd), Internal Audit (3rd) (MD&A s.7).
FCT per CIA standards and ORSA completed annually; Risk Appetite Policy, Capital Risk Policy and Capital & Liquidity Mgmt Framework approved by Board.
risk.capital_target: Internal capital targets above OSFI supervisory target; numeric range not disclosed. SLF LICAT 145% / SLA 133% at 2026-06-30 (157%/140% at 2025-12-31).
sensitivities: Interest rates +/-50bp: net income nil / -C$25m; LICAT (SLF) +3 / -3 points (2025-12-31).
Credit spreads +/-50bp: net income +C$125m / -C$25m; LICAT +/-2.5 points (2025-12-31).
hedging: Segregated-fund guarantee hedging program covers materially all in-force contracts (dynamic + static hedges).
Interest-rate swaps, swaptions and bond forwards for ALM duration/convexity; FX forwards on foreign subsidiaries' net investment.
Reinsurance and partnerships (Wilton Re) used for capital-intensive legacy/PRT blocks.
events: 2026: LICAT fell from 157% to 145% on BGO/Crescent buy-ups (~C$2.4bn) and buybacks - management says within appetite.
2026: Ocehan mini-tender offers for SLF shares (Jul, Oct 2026) - shareholder cautions issued; no regulatory action.
2025-26: CRO Tom Murphy moved to lead SLAM; Jacques Goulet CRO from 2026-01-01.
No regulatory enforcement actions identified in FY2025 AIF/MD&A.
